clue.text: Tree snake's setback in Gilbert's so-called ballads

indicators.note: in tells us the turned snake sits inside the ballads' name

parts.note: W. S. Gilbert's comic verses were published as the Bab Ballads, Bab being his childhood nickname

indicators.note: a setback sends the snake word backwards, so its letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A snake recoils in one of W. S. Gilbert's comic ballads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setback' turns BOA into AOB, and 'in' puts that inside BAB.
explanation.definitionFit: The baobab is a massive African tree with a swollen trunk.

clue.text: Union for everybody? A nice change

parts.note: all means everybody

indicators.note: change tells us to rearrange the letters of the words a nice

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a union for everybody would make a pleasant change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges A NICE into IANCE, which follows ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance is a joining of parties for common purpose, a synonym of union.

clue.text: In olden times a measure of game

indicators.note: In says the a sits inside the letters for olden times

parts.note: BC, before Christ, marks dates in olden times
taken as written
a carat is a measure of weight for gems or purity for gold

explanation.surface: A measure of some game played in olden times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' puts A inside BC to give BAC, then CARAT follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Baccarat is a card game played in casinos.

clue.text: New clock in the city is part of a set

indicators.note: in places the rearranged clock inside the city's name

parts.note: Bath is a city in Somerset, England, famous for its Roman baths

indicators.note: New signals that the letters of clock are made into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A new clock in town has been installed as part of a stage set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges CLOCK into CKCLO, and 'in' puts it inside BATH, an English city.
explanation.definitionFit: A backcloth is the painted curtain hung at the back of a theatre stage, part of the scenery.

clue.text: Weekly produced in six days

explanation.surface: A weekly paper was produced in under a week.
explanation.walkthrough: The Universe is a long-running Catholic weekly newspaper; Genesis has the cosmos made in six days.
explanation.definitionFit: The Universe is a Catholic weekly newspaper, and in Genesis all creation was made in six days.

clue.text: Speakers deplore this sort of language

definitions.text: Speakers deplore this sort of language

parts.words: Speakers deplore this sort of language
parts.note: the Speaker of the House of Commons rebukes members who use insulting words in debate

explanation.surface: Orators condemn a certain kind of vocabulary.
explanation.walkthrough: Speakers looks like people speaking generally, but it means the Speaker who chairs the Commons and rules on offensive remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: Language banned in Parliament, such as calling a member a liar, is officially disallowed by the Speaker.

clue.text: Whines are heard to issue from his premises

definitions.text: Whines are heard to issue from his premises

parts.words: Whines are heard to issue from his premises
parts.note: whines sounds like wines, so the premises are a shop selling drink

explanation.surface: Complaints can be heard coming from someone's building.
explanation.walkthrough: The whining is a pun: said out loud, it is wines, which flow from a wine merchant's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A vintner is a wine merchant, whose shop sends out bottles of drink.

clue.text: Form of eastern Braille that can be depended upon

indicators.note: Form of means a new form is made from these letters, rearranging them

explanation.surface: A kind of Braille from the East proves trustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form of' rearranges E and BRAILLE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reliable is trustworthy and dependable.

clue.text: One who really tries at English Literature?

definitions.text: One who really tries at English Literature?

parts.words: One who really tries at English Literature?
parts.note: an essay is literally an attempt or try, so a writer of short prose pieces makes tries

explanation.surface: A student who works hard at English Literature.
explanation.walkthrough: Tries looks like effort, but an essay (French essai) is literally an attempt.
explanation.definitionFit: An essayist writes essays, short literary compositions whose name means attempts.

clue.text: Bird once associated with judges

explanation.surface: A bird once linked with the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: The blackcap is a warbler, and British judges put on a black cap to pass a death sentence.

clue.text: Viewpoints of settlers from Schleswig-Holstein

explanation.surface: The opinions of colonists from northern Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Angles are perspectives, and the Angles were a Germanic tribe from Angeln in Schleswig who settled England.

clue.text: Scholarly cavalryman who can settle accounts

parts.note: a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a scholarly degree holder
a lancer is a mounted soldier armed with a lance

explanation.surface: A learned horse soldier who can also square the books.
explanation.walkthrough: BA is a graduate's degree, used here for a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: A balancer squares up figures so that debits and credits match.

clue.text: A foreign female asylum started for the disturbed

parts.note: une is French for a, in its feminine form

indicators.note: started means only the beginning of the word asylum is used, its end dropped

parts.note: taken as written before cutting

explanation.surface: A foreign woman sets up a refuge for the mentally disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started' keeps only the start of ASYLUM, giving ASY, with LUM dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Uneasy describes someone troubled or anxious in mind.

clue.text: The product of Rome, it's a fine sprayer

indicators.note: The product of says the letters are reworked to produce something new

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Rome makes a good spray device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The product of' rearranges ROME, ITS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser turns liquid such as perfume into a fine mist.

clue.text: Antony's friend — one upset by rail transport

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so the word one reads upwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
a bar is a rail
a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: Mark Antony's companion is knocked over by a rail vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ONE into ENO. Enobarbus is Antony's friend in Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra.
explanation.definitionFit: Enobarbus is Mark Antony's loyal follower in Shakespeare's Roman tragedy.

clue.text: Quietly consume vegetable matter

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: Eat your vegetables quietly.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is partly decayed plant material from bogs.

clue.text: Symphony written for old type of examination?

parts.note: past means old, gone by
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A symphony written for an old-fashioned exam.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Sixth Symphony is called the Pastoral.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Sixth Symphony is known by this name for its countryside scenes.

clue.text: Corydon, for one, was singularly musical

definitions.text: Corydon, for one, was singularly musical

parts.words: Corydon, for one, was singularly musical
parts.note: Virgil calls Corydon and Thyrsis 'Arcades ambo', both from the shepherds' land and both fine singers

explanation.surface: A shepherd named Corydon was remarkably gifted at music.
explanation.walkthrough: Singularly means remarkably on the surface, but also hints at the singular form of Virgil's plural Arcades.
explanation.definitionFit: Corydon is a pastoral shepherd-singer from Arcadia in Virgil's Eclogues, the idealised rural home of song.

clue.text: Party for an unfashionable six-footer

indicators.note: in means fashionable, so being unfashionable means losing the word in

parts.note: an insect has six legs

explanation.surface: A party for an unstylish tall person.
explanation.walkthrough: A six-footer looks like a tall person, but it is a six-legged insect; 'unfashionable' drops IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A sect is a faction or group, like a party.

clue.text: Paterfamilias supports son, young gangster

indicators.note: in a down clue the word that supports another sits beneath it

parts.note: the paterfamilias is the head of the family, or kin head

explanation.surface: A father provides for his son, who has become a teenage thug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts KINHEAD below S in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A skinhead is a youth of a shaven-headed street gang culture.

clue.text: Lawrence, following many, refused to recognize this saw

indicators.note: following puts the Lawrence word after the word for many

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross
to cut someone is to snub them

explanation.surface: Lawrence followed the crowd and snubbed what he saw.
explanation.walkthrough: Saw looks like a verb, but it is the tool. T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) used the alias Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: A crosscut saw cuts timber across the grain.

clue.text: Plant a counterfeit diamond

parts.note: sham means fake or counterfeit
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: Someone sneaks a fake diamond into place.
explanation.walkthrough: Plant looks like a verb (to conceal), but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a clover-like plant, emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: Resort seems first-class for a cat

indicators.note: Resort is read as re-sort, so the letters are sorted again into a new order

parts.note: A1 means first-class, with the 1 read as I

explanation.surface: A holiday resort seems excellent for a cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' rearranges SEEMS with AI (A1, first-class).
explanation.definitionFit: The Siamese is a breed of cat from Thailand.

clue.text: A star — one made for coronets

indicators.note: made here means made up, so these letters are formed into new words

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A celebrity had one crafted to wear as headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made' rearranges A STAR with I.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiaras are jewelled headbands, small crowns worn by women.

clue.text: Parsimony associated with neighbours

explanation.surface: Meanness goes with living next door.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearness means stinginess (being near) and closeness, which is what neighbours have.

clue.text: Horseman entraps a surprise attacker

indicators.note: entraps means it closes round the a, holding it inside

parts.note: a rider is a horseman

explanation.surface: A horseman catches a surprise assailant.
explanation.definitionFit: A raider makes sudden assaults or forays.

clue.text: Surroundings for a doctor in EEC assembly

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

indicators.note: assembly means the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Settings for a doctor working within the European Community.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges IN EEC into IENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambience is the atmosphere or setting of a place.

clue.text: Mildness of man that's North Carolina youth leader

parts.note: Len is a man's name
i.e., id est, means that is
NC is the US state abbreviation for North Carolina

indicators.note: the leader of youth is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gentle man who leads the youth of North Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' takes Y, the first letter of youth.
explanation.definitionFit: Leniency is gentleness or tolerance in judgement.

clue.text: Calm as some addressed at Ephesus

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Composed, like those St Paul wrote to at Ephesus.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Paul's Letter to the Ephesians.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedate means calm and unhurried.
